Extreme weather

Delhi Summer

Delhi's air conditioners need more power each summer. In the heat of 2024, coal and gas plants will produce less, and a late monsoon will prolong the shortage risk.

Play Delhi Summer↗ Your decisions ↓

Choose your difficulty before you start. It’s free to play in your browser.

Location
Delhi, India
Starts in
2018
Your term
7 years

Your starting point

You take over in 2018 with coal, gas, solar, wind and a small battery. Over seven years, each summer pushes demand higher.

Hot weather cuts the output of your coal and gas plants just when customers need them most. Look at which hours run short before you decide how to prepare.

Learn how to play

Your decisions

  1. 01

    Build between summers

    Check how much spare power you had at last year's peak. Will the next project finish before that margin is gone?

  2. 02

    Stretch solar past sunset

    Look for spare daytime solar power you could store. Check how long the battery can cover cooling demand into the evening.

  3. 03

    Reduce the peak

    Compare what it costs to reduce electricity use during a hot spell with the cost of running another plant.

How much cooling demand can you cover if the monsoon is late?
